title: If You Fell Into JUPITER, You'd Never Hit the Ground 🪐
description:
If you fell into Jupiter, you'd never hit the ground. Jupiter is a gas giant: it has no solid surface at all. Fall in, and the gas around you just keeps getting thicker and hotter as the pressure builds, until the hydrogen is squeezed into a hot liquid, with no surface to splash into. NASA really did drop a probe into Jupiter in 1995 (the Galileo probe): it sent back data for about 58 minutes before the heat and the pressure destroyed it. And deep inside, some scientists think it might even rain diamonds (an idea from 2013; nobody has seen it yet). Would you jump? Yes or no?
